methodology:
ALCO is mid-strategic-transformation — winding down its citrus operations and pivoting to a "diversified land company" model with revenue-sharing arrangements (citrus growers, cattle, mining, sugarcane, sod). The 49,537-acre portfolio spans 8 Florida counties with three use categories (citrus 39,297; land mgmt 9,583; mining 657).

The Properties table below shows one row per county aggregating all three use types within that county. The 10-K Item 2 disclosure provides this exact county × use breakdown. Per-property FMV is computed as a weighted blend by use × county-specific FMV/acre.

Primary comp anchors, all dated within the last 24 months:
- ALCO's own January 2026 dispositions: 2,950 Hendry-County citrus acres at $9,085/acre and 579 Polk-County acres at $10,535/acre — directly observed transactions, the most defensible reference.
- ASFMRA Florida 2025 citrus mid-cycle benchmark $8,500/acre (greening-discounted).
- USDA NASS 2024 + 2025 Florida cropland.
- Collier County (Naples MSA) carries an embedded development-optionality premium because of urban encroachment around Naples; recent rural-to-development conversions in Collier have transacted at $20-30K/acre. The 4,757 land-mgmt acres in Collier mark up to $25K/acre to reflect that.

The book value is a rough estimate from net PP&E ($142M total) allocated by acre and use type — ALCO doesn't publish farm-by-farm book; refining this against the 10-K balance sheet is a useful follow-up. The FMV calculation is most sensitive to the Collier development premium and the citrus benchmark; sensitivity analysis would be useful.
